# NUMBER-PARSE-PATTERN v1.2 routes, the rows of PR #2215: which implementation decides each literal shape of Double.parseDouble / Float.parseFloat
# in java.base on this branch. route M3 = the absorbed FastDoubleParser atoms decide; route JDK = the original FloatingDecimal converter decides (a decimal
# literal whose exponent number reached the clamp reaches the decimal kernel with DECLINED_EXPONENT, so it returns NaN and valueOfFloatLiteral calls
# FloatingDecimal.readJavaFormatString; a grammar rejection throws and the wiring catches IllegalArgumentException). Line numbers name the pre-image
# a5d6cc2a79c (atoms and hashes: DEC_ATOMS_PR2215.tsv). The hexadecimal shapes (rows HEX_* of PR #2245, HEX_ROUTE v1) are one row here: on this
# branch the donor's hex path still decides every hex literal.

column5: PR #2215 (FastDoubleParser 1.0.90 hex path, unchanged by DEC_EXPONENT_CLAMP v1)
column6: RESIDUE (OPEN on this branch): three defects of the donor's hex path (an unsigned significand >= 2^63 rounded twice, no sticky bit for the digits the re-parse drops, the exponent number clamped before the fraction digits are subtracted: 0x.1p10240 gives 2^1020 instead of Infinity); PR #2245 (HEX_ROUTE v1) routes every hex literal to the JDK and lands with this PR

column3: every decimal literal without an exponent or with an exponent number below MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER (1024)
column5: PR #2215; DEC_EXPONENT_CLAMP v1 changed only the two parseDecFloatLiteral templates, and in them only a decline block before the kernel call (DEC_BYTECODE_METHOD_DELTA.tsv: every other method of the 24 classes instruction-identical)
column7: M3ParseDifferential diff 600000 sha256 233e0f59... on stock, pre-image and post-image; decimal differential (DEC_DIFFERENTIAL v1) categories GENERAL, CLAMP_FINITE and UNCLAMPED_HIGH identical on pre-image and post-image; verifier corpus seed 0x5EED2245 (200,000 decimal literals) identical to stock on the post-image; PERF_GATE_DEC_PR2215.tsv

column3: decimal literal whose exponent number reaches MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER: the exponent loop stops multiplying at 1024 (10240 parses as 1024, 100000 as 10000, 2147483648 as 2147), and the digit counts are added afterwards, in both directions: fraction digits ("0." + 723 zeros + "1e10240", "0." + 9999 zeros + "1e100000") and integer digits beyond the 19 the re-parse keeps ("1" + 1100 zeros + "e-10240", "1" + 800 zeros + "e-10240"); also every exponent number of 1024 to 10239 that was not clamped
column5: DEC_EXPONENT_CLAMP v1 (the same change as PR #2245 9f6d5f3f9f7, now on the base): parseDecFloatLiteral passes DECLINED_EXPONENT (Integer.MIN_VALUE) as both exponents, outside the decimal range of both kernels (double [-325, 308], float [-45, 38]), so the kernel declines and valueOfFloatLiteral calls FloatingDecimal.readJavaFormatString
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern, fixed by routing): a saturating accumulator feeds a later adjustment, so the adjustment can bring a saturated value back into range; M3 gave 1e300 (0x7e37e43c8800759c), 1.0 (0x3ff0000000000000), 1e76 (0x4fb61bcca7119916) and about 1e-224 (0x116d9ca79d89462a) where the JDK gives Infinity, Infinity, 0.0 and 0.0. An exact M3 route would accumulate the exponent number past the clamp and saturate after the digit counts (candidate DEC_EXACT_M3; not needed, the shape is rare)
